title: Unbounded degree overhead for Alice-conditioned quantum Bell certificates
abstract: Requiring each sum-of-squares term to involve only one of Alice's measurement questions can impose an unbounded certification cost. In the simplest Bell scenario, we prove that no finite level of the Alice-conditioned NPA hierarchy contains all standard level-two Bell certificates. An explicit family of truncated positive functionals on the infinite dihedral group exceeds the tilted-CHSH quantum bound at every prescribed finite level, while a standard degree-two certificate is exact. A Fejer-weighted trace reduces positivity to a rank-one subtraction from a moving-average Gram matrix. The required conditioned level grows at least as $(2-α)^{-1/2}$ near the endpoint tilt. This bounds the degree of exact nice-SOS inputs to compiled-game soundness proofs. Consequently, no finite conditioned level certifies the entire optimal CHSH randomness tradeoff against quantum side information, although standard level two does. Away from the endpoint, we prove a sharp one-level cost throughout $α\in[13/10,3/2]$, using optimal-strategy kernels and exact Bernstein matrix positivity to certify a continuous interval. The results separate ordinary SOS degree from the resources keyed by single-question certificate structure.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the resource cost of certifying quantum Bell inequalities when measurements are conditioned on one party's outcomes. It proves that this conditioning imposes an unbounded overhead in the required algebraic degree compared to standard certification methods. The work significantly separates the complexity of standard quantum bounds from those requiring single-question structure.
main_problem: The paper investigates the resource overhead required to certify quantum Bell inequalities when conditioning the test on one party's measurements (Alice-conditioned certificates). It aims to compare this overhead against standard certification methods.
main_result: The required certification degree for Alice-conditioned certificates grows unboundedly as the Bell test approaches certain endpoints, demonstrating a separation between the resources needed for standard versus conditioned certification.
method: The authors use the framework of the NPA hierarchy, formulating the problem as a Sum-of-Squares (SOS) decomposition problem, and employ techniques like Fejér-weighted traces and Gram matrix analysis.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum Bell inequalities, specifically using the CHSH scenario, and analyzing the required levels of the NPA hierarchy to certify quantum correlations.
key_observables: The primary observables are the minimum required certificate levels ($d_{std}$ vs. $d_{os}$) and the resulting bounds on the CHSH expectation value ($s$).
important_parameters: The parameter $\alpha$ controls the specific Bell test instance, and the analysis examines behavior near endpoint tilts ($\epsilon 	o 0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the optimal certificate lies on the boundary of the PSD cone, and it distinguishes between numerical saturation fits and true exact upper bounds.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the divergence of the required conditioned degree (purple staircase) from the standard, fixed degree line as the test parameter approaches an endpoint.
paper_structure: The paper develops results by first establishing the unbounded overhead for conditioned certificates (Theorem 1), then characterizing finite exactness intervals (Theorem 2), and finally providing rigorous, solver-free verification of these optimal bounds.
why_interesting: It provides deep theoretical insights into the limitations of polynomial methods (like SOS/NPA) to capture the full complexity of quantum correlations, which is fundamental to quantum information theory.
